newsitem.title: GERMANY: Karstadt shares up, takeover talk persists.
newsitem.headline: Karstadt shares up, takeover talk persists.

text.p: Shares in German retail firm Karstadt AG surged on Wednesday as speculation that the WCM holding group was poised to buy a large stake in the company persisted despite repeated denials from WCM.

The topic of the day in an otherwise dull trading session was the chance that WCM would acquire a significant holding in Karstadt, largely by taking over large stakes in the company from top German banks.
The story, which has been a recurrent theme in German media in recent weeks, resurfaced in the Platow Brief bourse newsletter on Wednesday.
Although WCM dismissed the report as "pure speculation", interest in Karstadt was high.
The share hit an alltime high of 654 marks during bourse trade, marking a jump of nearly four percent, and ended the session at 650 marks. The broader DAX index was up 0.34 percent.
"The longer these rumours go on, the more credence everyone is attaching to them," said one Frankfurt dealer of the WCM story.
"The banks have not issued a firm denial and that is as good as a confirmation as far as many people are concerned. And the deal would make perfect sense," he added.
Another dealer noted that Karstadt was due a period in the limelight as it had been left out of the recent surge to record highs on the DAX.
Karstadt's jump above 640 marks was a technical buy signal, he said.
While Karstadt's latest advance has brought it up to speed with broader market gains, the share was trading above 670 marks last September.
Bank in Liechtenstein earlier this week set a six-month target for Karstadt shares of 750 to 800 marks.
